answer: Next-hop data is keyed by RIB because each next-hop entry represents a RIB identified by the 'name' key, and all routes in a RIB belong to the same address family. For each routing instance the system provides one system-controlled default RIB per supported address family, so the RIB name is what pins a next hop to an address family. Syntax: show next-hop-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix>/<interface> [next-hop-address]. rib-name is a String of length 1..64 (pattern '([A-Za-z0-9 -.,]*)'), destination-prefix is an IP prefix, interface is the outgoing interface reference (for example DCN), and next-hop-address is an IPv4 or IPv6 address. Available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: show next-hop-IPv4/0.0.0.0/0/DCN.

Use clear [-f] ospf [instance=]<value>. It removes and restarts an ospf-instance, and the operation is asynchronous, so the CLI does not wait for the restart to complete. The instance parameter is the id of the ospf-instance, given as a string, and it must be supplied. The -f flag forces the command without confirmation; without it you are prompted to confirm. Access mode is Operational Mode only. Example: clear ospf 1. The ospf-instance command description points at clear for removing an OSPF instance from the configuration asynchronously.

No. ospf-area-type accepts only the value normal, and normal is also the default, so stub and NSSA area types are not offered. Areas are managed with add / set / show / delete ospf-area-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id> [ospf-area-type <value>], where instance-id is uint8 in range 0..255 and ospf-area-id is a dotted-quad. The pre-condition is that the OSPF instance must be created before the area can be added. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add ospf-area-1/0.0.0.0.

Use the ospf-area-range commands: add / set / show / delete ospf-area-range-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<prefix> [advertise <value>]. This summarizes routes for an OSPF area matching address/mask, and it is applicable to Area Border Routers (ABRs) only, so it has no effect on a non-ABR. advertise takes true or false and defaults to true (true advertises the summary, false hides it). The prefix may be an IPv4 prefix (length up to 32) or an IPv6 prefix (length up to 128), in canonical form with non-prefix bits zero. Pre-condition: the OSPF instance must be created before the area can be added. Example: add ospf-area-range-1/9.9.9.9/10.220.0.0/16 advertise true.

Yes. ospf-instance has a version attribute with values ospfv2 and ospfv3, defaulting to ospfv2; version is settable only on add (it is not in the set syntax). Router id is chosen by router-id-mode, which takes manual or use-loopback and defaults to use-loopback; with use-loopback the pre-condition is that an ipv4 LO-MGMT address must be configured. With manual you supply router-id as a dotted-quad. instance-id is uint8 in range 0..255 and description is a String of length 0..128. show also exposes vrf. Example: add ospf-instance-2 description xyz router-id-mode use-loopback version ospfv3.

On ospf-interface the defaults are hello-interval 10 seconds (uint16, range 1..32767) and router-dead-interval 40 seconds (uint16, range 4..65535). Related defaults: retransmission-interval 5 s (2..3600), transmit-delay 1 s (1..450), ospf-cost 10 (1..65535), priority 1 (0..255, where 0 means not eligible for DR or BDR), enable true, ospf-if-routing auto (active, passive, auto). Yes, you can authenticate: ospf-auth-enable is true/false with default false and is relevant for ospfv2 or ospfv3; ospf-auth-algorithm is none or HMAC_SHA_256 with default HMAC_SHA_256, and ospf-auth-key is an ASCII string of length 0..256, both relevant for ospfv2 only. Pre-condition: the OSPF instance and OSPF area must exist first.

Use show ospf-neighbor-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<ospf-if-name>/<router-id> [state] [role] [address] [priority] in Operational Mode. The state values are: down (initial, no Hello packets received), init (Hellos received but bidirectional communication not yet established), 2-way (bidirectional established, DR/BDR election occurs here), exstart (DR and BDR elected, master-slave relation determined), exchange (neighbors exchange DataBaseDescriptor packets with LSA headers), loading (full Link State information exchanged based on DBDs) and full (full adjacency achieved). The role values are drother (Designated Router Other), dr (Designated Router), bdr (Backup Designated Router) and ptp (point-to-point). Note that an OSPF neighbor is deleted when the OSPF interface is down.

Use add ospfv3-ipsec-security-association-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<ospf-if-name>/<spi> integrity-algorithm <value> [ipsec-protocol <value>] [ipsec-mode <value>], with matching set, show and delete forms. spi is a unique uint32 security parameter index in range 256..4294967295. integrity-algorithm is mandatory on add and accepts AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128, AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_384_192, AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_512_256, AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_160 and AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96. ipsec-protocol indicates ESP or AH, with ESP as the value and default. ipsec-mode supports transport only, default transport. Pre-condition: the OSPF instance must be created first. Example: add ospfv3-ipsec-security-association-1/0.0.0.0/DCN/256 integrity-algorithm AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128.

Use ping [-c=<count>] [-w=<timeout>] [-s=<pktsize>] [-i=<interface> | -v=<vrf>] <ping-dest>. -i=<interface> specifies the source interface; by default the interface is selected according to the routing table. -v=<vrf> specifies the VRF; by default the MGMT VRF is used. The interface and VRF name parameters are mutually exclusive, so you pick one or the other. -c stops after sending count ECHO_REQUEST packets, -w gives a timeout in seconds before ping exits regardless of packets sent or received, and -s sets the payload octets excluding headers, default 56, plus 8 octets of ICMP header for a total packet size of 64 octets. ping-dest may be an ipv4-address, ipv6-address or domain-name. Example: ping -c=1 -w=10 -s=1024 192.0.2.3.

Use show protocols, which lists them all in one place: ssh, cli, serial-console, netconf, restconf, grpc, snmp, http-file-server and data-model-openconfig. You can drill into any one with show protocols <name>, for example show protocols ssh. Typical attributes shown: ssh has enabled, port 8022, host keys and pre/post-login messages; cli enabled true, port 22, script-dir '/storage/scripts'; serial-console global-switch and global-timeout 60 minutes; netconf enabled true, port 830; restconf enabled true, http-enabled false, https-enabled true, http-port 8080, https-port 8181, cookie-timeout 5 minutes, api-root '/restconf'; grpc enabled true, port 50051; snmp enabled true, port 161, snmp-engine-id; http-file-server http-port 8980, https-port 8981, url-base '/transfer'. Available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use show rib-<rib-name> [vrf] [address-family]. Each entry represents a RIB identified by the 'name' key, and all routes in a RIB belong to the same address family; for each routing instance the system provides one system-controlled default RIB for each supported address family, so selecting the RIB selects the address family. rib-name is a String of length 1..64, vrf is a leafref to the VRF the RIB is bound to (path '../../vrf/name'), and address-family takes ipv4-unicast or ipv6-unicast. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: show rib-IPv4 displays the RIB identified by the 'IPv4' key.

Use show route-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix> [special-next-hop] [source-protocol]. The command shows the list of system routes from various sources, such as dynamic protocols and static route, and the source-protocol attribute gives the source protocol for the route entry, for example OSPF, BGP or static. rib-name is a String of length 1..64 and destination-prefix is an IPv4 or IPv6 address. The special-next-hop attribute takes none, blackhole or unreachable with default none: none is normal routes, while for blackhole and unreachable routes no next-hop is created under the route. It applies to IPv4 and IPv6 static routes, rib:routes and IP Monitoring. Example: show route.

Yes. show routing displays the routing information. It takes no parameters at all, and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For the detail underneath it, use the related commands: show rib-<rib-name> [vrf] [address-family] for RIB entries per address family, show route-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix> [special-next-hop] [source-protocol] for the system routes and their source protocol, show next-hop-<rib-name>/<destination-prefix>/<interface> [next-hop-address] for next hops, and show vrf-<name> [type] [chassis-name] [description] for the routing instances.

show supporting-interface-<name>/<interface> displays supporting interface information, that is, which underlying IPv4/IPv6 interface supports a given interface. The name parameter is the name of the interface (string), and the interface parameter is a reference to the IPv4/IPv6 interface, expressed as the path ../../../../../networking/interface/if-name. It is a show-only command with no add, set or delete form, and it is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. So it tells you the supporting interface relationship for an interface: the interface name you ask about, and the networking interface if-name that supports it. Running show supporting-interface without a key lists the supporting-interface entries.

Syntax: traceroute [-m=<hopcnt>] [-w=<timeout>] [-i=<interface> | -v=<vrf>] <tr-dest> [pktsize]. The maximum number of hops (-m, the max time-to-live value) defaults to 30, with a range of 1..255 (uint8). The VRF is set with -v=<vrf>; if not provided it defaults to MGMT. -i=<interface> sets the source interface, and by default the interface is selected according to the routing table; the interface and VRF name parameters are mutually exclusive. -w=<timeout> defaults to 2 seconds, range 1..10 (uint16). pktsize is the total probing packet size, default 60 (60 bytes for IPv4). tr-dest may be an IPv4 address, IPv6 address or domain-name. Example: traceroute -m=10 -w=3 1.2.3.4.

Use show vrf-<name> [type] [chassis-name] [description], which shows the Virtual Routing and Forwarding (VRF) instance. name is the VRF name, a String of length 0..32. type gives the VRF type with values mgmt (Management VRF) and internal (Internal VRF). chassis-name gives the associated chassis name for that VRF, which is how you see which chassis each instance belongs to. description is a String of length 0..255 describing the VRF and its intended purpose. Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Example: show vrf-MGMT displays the Management VRF attributes.

Use activate [-f] swimage [label <string>] [db-action <empty-db|upgrade-db|rollback|auto>]. A successful swimage activation implies a system restart, so yes, the node restarts. The optional db-action parameter specifies the action applied to the database on activation: auto (the default) processes the database with the system default behavior, empty-db activates with an empty database, upgrade-db activates by upgrading the current database, and rollback rolls back to the previous active software image. If db-action is not provided the system decides automatically. Unless the -f option is given, the user must confirm the activation when prompted. label specifies the sw image/manifest file name; if not specified, the currently installable image is used. Examples: activate swimage db-action=empty-db, activate -f swimage.

No. Only a single location led test can be running at a time, so you cannot flash two cards simultaneously. Use activate location-led [entity=]<value> [[timeout=]<value>] [[led-mode=]<value>], where entity is a chassis or a card. led-mode is flash (default), an amber light blinking at 1 Hz used for LED location, or solid, a steady amber light used for lamp test; in lamp test all chassis LEDs light amber. timeout is a number in the range 0..120 seconds, default 0, which means no timer and the function runs until stopped. To turn it off, use terminate location-led <entity>; invoking it when no test is active has no effect. Note that the timeout parameter does not take effect in 1830 GX G30 R5.1, so terminate must be used, and not all cards support the Location LED test.

Use bootstrap ([local-port=]<value> | [neighbor-address=]<value>) [new-admin-user=]<value> [new-password=]<value>. It bootstraps a neighbor NE by establishing a TLS connection over the OSC link and provisioning the initial administrator account, for use during commissioning when the OSC peer NE has no configured users yet. Select the neighbor either with local-port, the supporting-port of an osc-eth MGMT interface as shown by show interface (for example 1-1-dwdm-line1), or with neighbor-address, the IPv6 link-local address of the OSC peer including zone (string length 7..256, pattern 'fe80:.*'). With local-port the system maps it to the OCE netdev (OCE-<chassis>-<slot>-<vlan-id>) and resolves the peer address via get_osc_neighbors.sh; if resolution fails the RPC is rejected. new-admin-user is mandatory, length 1..32, and follows local user naming rules. new-password may be plain text (standard complexity rules apply) or a SHA512 hash ($6$<salt>$<hash>, salt 2..16 chars). Available in Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Type cancel-upgrade. That is the whole command; the only flag is -h, which displays help for the command. It cancels any active upgrade in progress. Access mode is Operational mode, and the pre-condition is that an upgrade must be in progress for the command to execute successfully, so if nothing is running the command will not execute successfully. There are no other parameters, no entity or target to name, and no force flag. To see the state of the upgrade before or after cancelling, use show upgrade-status.

change-ztp-mode enabled starts ZTP, reverts the database to the factory default and triggers a system reboot, so on an in-service node you lose the configuration and the node reboots. The syntax is change-ztp-mode [-f] [ztp-mode=]<value>, where ztp-mode takes enabled or disabled and there is no default; -f forces the command without confirmation, so without it you are prompted. change-ztp-mode disabled disables ZTP and stops ZTP if it is already in progress; the command can be executed while ZTP is running, interrupting it. Access mode is Operational mode. The current ZTP mode configuration is displayed with show ztp.

Use show current-fw, which lists the current firmware available in the cards, or narrow it with forms such as show current-fw-<card-name>-<port-name>/<fw-name>, show current-fw-<card-name>.<slot-name>/<fw-name>, show current-fw-<chassis-name>-<slot-name>/<fw-name> or show current-fw-<name>/<fw-name>, each accepting [fw-version] [expected-fw-version] [fw-status]. Compare fw-version (current version, String 0..32) against expected-fw-version (String 0..32); fw-status states it directly, with values current (firmware is up-to-date), not-current (current firmware is not up-to-date against the expected one) and unavailable (firmware status information is currently unavailable), default unavailable. fw-name is a String of length 0..32. Example: show current-fw-1-3/DCO_1.

download supports these filetype values: crl (a CRL file in PEM format), database (a previously uploaded database), file (any file to the file-system), krp (key replacement package), local-certificate (PKCS#12 with password-protected private key, or PKCS#7 if pending-import), peer-certificate (X.509v3 PKCS#12), script (a CLI script), swimage (downloads a manifest file then all files belonging to a SW image) and trusted-certificate (X.509v3 PKCS#7 Root or Intermediate CA). The system automatically stores the downloaded file in an appropriate place, so no local location is needed; use show transfer to see the default storage directory. The exception is filetype file, where the destination parameter may be omitted (default directory, original name), a file-name only, a relative path or an absolute path, and you need write access to it. A downloaded database is stored as a db-instance=temp database, overwriting any existing temp. Source is a file-server plus path, or a URL using ftp, sftp, scp, http, https or file; ftp and http require secure-mode disabled.

Use show downloaded-image-<manifest-file>/<name> [signature], which retrieves information about downloaded image files. manifest-file is the downloaded manifest file (String, length 0..256), name is the name of the downloaded software image (String, length 0..256), and signature is the downloaded software image file signature (String, length 0..1024). Running show downloaded-image with no key shows all the downloaded software image files. Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

show downloads shows a list of downloads. It takes no parameters, and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Related commands: show downloaded-image-<manifest-file>/<name> [signature] retrieves information about downloaded image files including the file signature, and show transfer-status gives the progress of a transfer started asynchronously with download -a.
